Gunsilius computes a separate optimal weight in each pre-period and averages those weights, then assumes the resulting weight remains optimal post-treatment; causal identification is justified through scaled-isometry or weight-preserving evolution conditions. Its basic estimation class permits arbitrary finite-second-moment laws, while Proposition 5 adds finite supports and asymptotically balanced cell sizes with the pre-estimated weight treated as fixed.
